newsitem.title: USA: H.J. Heinz reports slight earnings gain.
newsitem.headline: H.J. Heinz reports slight earnings gain.

text.p: H.J. Heinz Company, after earlier warning that its latest results would be lower than expected, reported slightly higher quarterly profits Tuesday.
But the results were still below Wall Street's expectations.
Heinz said it earned $179.5 million in its fiscal first quarter, up from $174.5 million last year.
The earnings were equal to 48 cents per share, up 4.3 percent from 46 cents per share in the same period last year, but below analysts' expectations of 51 cents a share.

Heinz said last month that its first-quarter earnings would be lower than expected because it ended a sales discounting policy to retailers, which led to declines in sales of some products, such as retail frozen potatoes and infant food overseas.

However, net sales for the quarter, which ended July 31, increased 5.5 percent to $2.21 billion from $2.09 billion. The company said revenues were helped by the aquisition of pet food, infant food, food service and tuna companies.

Heinz's results were also affected by the divestitures of several non-strategic businesses, including an overseas mushroom business, Weight Watchers Magazine, an overseas sweetener business, a powdered beverage business in South America and two regional dry pet food product lines.
Heinz stock was off 37.5 cents at $31.375 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
